title: Construction auger
prompt: A labelled scale teaching adaptation of the page 67 construction auger hangs from an external lifting support over a deep clear-sided soil box. Drill rotates and lowers the short auger so its cutting end loosens soil and the flights fill. Lift raises the filled auger clear. Empty removes the soil at the surface as an external operation before the next drilling cycle. Repeated cycles deepen the same hole. Show the shaft, cutting end, helical flights and carried soil. The support and soil box are teaching fixtures; do not add an automatic continuous spoil conveyor.
chapter: Part 1: The Mechanics of Movement / Screws
blurb: A scale teaching adaptation shows a short auger filling with soil, lifting and emptying between batches that deepen one hole.
adaptation: External lifting and rotary support, a clear-sided soil box and surface soil removal are teaching fixtures and operations, not additional auger anatomy.
truthNotes: Finite short rigid flights fill once per drilling batch.
External lifting and emptying are required before the next batch.
Removed soil persists on the flights or in the surface tray.
Stable soft-soil hole and illustrative scale geometry; not a literal book reproduction.
No crane drive, hidden motor, telescoping flights or continuous spoil conveyor.
1988 remains inaccessible and unverified; no edition-union claim.
